paragraphs: We are an integrated, growth-oriented services company focused on providing products and services to our customers primarily in the oil and natural gas, aviation and utility infrastructure industries. Our primary business objective is to drive returns through improved execution by prioritizing asset utilization, margin expansion, and capital efficiency across the portfolio. Our suite of services includes rental services, infrastructure services, natural sand proppant services, accommodation services and drilling services. Our rental services segment provides a wide range of equipment used in oilfield, construction and aviation activities. Our infrastructure services division provides engineering, design, construction, upgrade, maintenance and repair services to the fiber industry. Our natural sand proppant services division mines, processes and sells natural sand proppant used for hydraulic fracturing. Our drilling services segment provides directional drilling to oilfield operators. We believe that the services we offer play a critical role in increasing the ultimate recovery and present value of production streams from unconventional resources as well as in constructing and improving fiber network. Our complementary suite of services provides us with the opportunity to cross-sell our services and expand our customer base and geographic positioning.

We continue to focus on growing our rental business. We believe our portfolio of aviation assets provides an attractive form of aviation asset financing for operators that allows capital deployment and fleet flexibility while eliminating residual value risk for the operators.
Our facilities and service centers are strategically located in Ohio, Texas, Oklahoma, Wisconsin and Alberta, Canada primarily to serve the following areas:
•Eastern Ohio; •Southern Ohio; •West Texas; •The Appalachian Basin in the Northeast; •The SCOOP and STACK in Oklahoma;
•The Arkoma Basin in Arkansas and Oklahoma; •The Anadarko Basin in Oklahoma; •The Marcellus Shale in West Virginia and Pennsylvania;
•Southeastern New Mexico; •The Barnett Shale in Texas; •The Granite Wash and Mississippi Shale in Oklahoma and Texas;
•The Cana Woodford and Woodford Shales and the Cleveland Sand in Oklahoma; and

Our operational division heads have an extensive track record with an average of over 29 years of services experience. They bring valuable expertise and long-term customer relationships to our business. We provide our rental services, infrastructure services, natural sand proppant, accommodation services and drilling services to a diversified range of both public and private independent oil and natural gas producers, sand suppliers, fiber network owners and aircraft-based passenger and cargo providers.

Our revenues, operating income (loss) and identifiable assets are primarily attributable to five reportable segments: rental services, infrastructure services, natural sand proppant services, accommodation services, and drilling services.

Our equipment rental services provide a wide range of equipment used in drilling, flowback and hydraulic fracturing services as well as in construction activities. Our equipment rentals consist of cranes, light plants, generators and other oilfield related equipment. We provide equipment rental in West Texas, Eastern Ohio, Pennsylvania and West Virginia.

Our aviation services include leasing aircraft and aircraft equipment to customers. Aircraft equipment is comprised of auxiliary power units ("APUs") and engines. As of December 31, 2025, we owned nine regional aircraft, two helicopters, five jet engines, and ten APUs.

Our infrastructure services business provides engineering, design, construction, upgrade, maintenance and repair services to fiber networks. We provide infrastructure services primarily in the southwest and midwest portions of the United States.

Since we commenced operations in this line of business, a substantial portion of our infrastructure revenue has been generated from storm restoration work, primarily from the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority, or PREPA, due to damage caused by Hurricane Maria. On October 19, 2017, Cobra Acquisitions LLC, or Cobra, and PREPA entered into an emergency master services agreement for repairs to PREPA's electrical grid. The one-year contract, as amended, provided for payments of up to $945 million. On May 26, 2018, Cobra and PREPA entered into a second one-year, $900 million master services agreement to provide additional repair services and begin the initial phase of reconstruction of the electrical power system in Puerto Rico. Our work under each of the contracts with PREPA ended on March 31, 2019. PREPA is currently subject to bankruptcy proceedings, which were filed in July 2017 and are currently pending in the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico (the "Title III Court"). As a result, PREPA's ability to meet its payment obligations under the above-referenced agreements was largely dependent upon funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency ("FEMA") or other sources. Since September 30, 2019, Cobra has been pursuing litigation in the Title III Court and other dispute resolution efforts seeking recovery of the amounts owed to Cobra by PREPA for restoration services in Puerto Rico, which proceedings are discussed in more detail in the Company's prior reports filed with the SEC. PREPA was holding approximately $18.4 million in funds (the "Withheld FEMA Funds") received from FEMA and considered payable to Cobra but had been withheld due to garnishments asserted by three Puerto Rican municipalities (the "Specified Municipalities") for certain municipal tax claims discussed in Mammoth's filings with the SEC (the "Specified Municipal Tax Claims") and for which Cobra disputed any valid garnishment.

On July 22, 2024, Cobra entered into a release and settlement agreement with PREPA and the Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico ("FOMB"), in its capacity as Title III representative for PREPA, to settle all outstanding matters between Cobra and PREPA (the "Settlement Agreement"). Under the terms of the Settlement Agreement, Cobra was allowed an administrative expense claim against PREPA of $170.0 million, plus the $18.4 million in the Withheld FEMA Funds. Cobra's allowed claim will be paid through three installments: (i) $150.0 million on the later of (A) ten business days following approval of the Settlement Agreement by the Title III Court and (B) August 31, 2024; (ii) $20.0 million within seven days following the effective date of PREPA's plan of adjustment; and (iii) $18.4 million (subject to providing one or more indemnity letters of credit) in the Withheld FEMA Funds within either (A) ten business days after the deadline for appealing the entry of the settlement order by the Title III Court under the applicable bankruptcy rules of procedure if no such appeal is filed, or (B) if the provisions of the settlement order allowing PREPA to release the Withheld FEMA Funds to Cobra without retaining any liability to the Specified Municipalities are appealed by the Specified Municipalities, within ten business days of the filing of the notice of such appeal.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and the Industries We Serve
Our customer base is concentrated and the loss of one or more of our significant customers, or their failure to pay the amounts they owe us, could cause our revenue to decline substantially.
We may experience losses in excess of our recorded reserves for receivables.
Our revolving credit facility impose restrictions on us that may affect our ability to successfully operate our business.
The cyclicality of the oil and natural gas industry may cause our operating results to fluctuate.
If oil prices or natural gas prices decline, the demand for our oil and natural gas services could be adversely affected.
Failure to effectively and timely address the energy transition to a lower carbon footprint could adversely affect our oil and gas business.
Shortages, delays in delivery and interruptions in supply of major components, replacement parts or, other equipment, supplies or materials may adversely affect our rental business.
Advancements in oilfield service technologies could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
Our business depends upon our ability to obtain specialized equipment and parts from third-party suppliers, and we may be vulnerable to delayed deliveries and future price increases.

We may not accurately estimate the costs associated with infrastructure services provided under fixed price contracts, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

We may be unable to obtain sufficient bonding capacity to support certain service offerings, and the need for performance and surety bonds could reduce availability under our revolving credit facility.
The nature of our infrastructure services business exposes us to potential liability for warranty claims and faulty engineering, which may reduce our profitability.
The timing of new contracts and termination of existing contracts may result in unpredictable fluctuations in our cash flows and financial results.
Inaccuracies in estimates of volumes and qualities of our sand reserves could result in lower than expected sales and higher than expected production costs.
Demand for our frac sand products could be reduced by changes in well stimulation processes and technologies, as well as changes in governmental regulations and other applicable law.
We face distribution and logistics challenges in our business.
Increasing transportation and related costs could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Diminished access to water and inability to secure or maintain necessary permits may adversely affect operations of our frac sand processing plants.

The customized nature, and remote location, of the modular camps that we provide and service present unique challenges that could adversely affect our ability to successfully operate our remote accommodations business.
Health and food safety issues and food-borne illness concerns could adversely affect our remote accommodations business.
Development of permanent infrastructure in the Canadian oil sands region or other locations where we locate our remote accommodations could negatively impact our remote accommodations business.
Revenue generated and expenses incurred by our remote accommodation business are denominated in the Canadian dollar and could be negatively impacted by currency fluctuations.
In the course of our business, we may become subject to lawsuits, indemnity or other claims, which could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and cash flows.
We rely on a few key employees whose absence or loss could adversely affect our business.
If we are unable to employ a sufficient number of skilled and qualified workers, our capacity and profitability could be diminished and our growth potential could be impaired.
Unionization efforts could increase our costs or limit our flexibility.
Concerns over general economic, business or industry conditions may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity and financial condition.
paragraphs: Described below are certain risks that we believe apply to our business and the industries in which we operate. You should carefully consider each of the risks described below in conjunction with other information including the financial statements and related notes provided in this Annual Report and in our other public disclosures. The risks described below highlight potential events, trends or other circumstances that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, liquidity, and consequently, the market value of our common stock. These risks could cause our future results to differ materially from historical results and from guidance we may provide regarding our expectations of future financial performance. The risks described below are those that we have identified as material and is not an exhaustive list of all the risks we face. There may be other risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial which may also materially and adversely affect our business operations in the future. Please refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitation on forward-looking statements set forth on page iv hereof.

When a major customer discontinues the use our services, our revenue will decline and our operating results and financial condition will be harmed unless such loss is offset by new business. Our top five customers accounted for approximately 55% and 58%, respectively, of our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. It is likely that we will continue to derive a significant portion of our revenue from a relatively small number of customers in the future. In addition, we are subject to credit risk due to the concentration of our customer base. Any nonperformance by our counterparties, including their failure to pay the amounts they owe us on a timely basis or at all, either as a result of changes in financial and economic conditions or otherwise, could have a material adverse impact on our operating results and could adversely affect our liquidity.

We evaluate the collectability of our receivables based on consideration of a customer's ability to make required payments, payment history, economic events and other factors. Recorded reserves represent our estimate of current expected credit losses on existing receivables and are determined based on historical customer reviews, current financial conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. An unexpected change in customer financial condition or future economic uncertainty could result in additional requirements for specific reserves, which could have a material effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

We cannot predict the impact of the ongoing war in Ukraine, the instability in the Middle East and actions by the United States in Venezuela on the global economy, energy markets, geopolitical stability, industries in which we operate and our business.

Broader consequences of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict, instability in the Middle East and actions by the United States in Venezuela may increase volatility in the price and demand for oil and natural gas, which would adversely impact the oilfield services industry, increase exposure to cyberattacks, cause disruptions in global supply chains, increase foreign currency fluctuations, cause constraints or disruption in the capital markets and limit sources of liquidity. We cannot predict the extent of these wars' effect on our business and results of operations as well as on the global economy, energy markets and industries in which we operate.

Cobra was party to service contracts with PREPA. Due to PREPA's bankruptcy proceedings, PREPA's ability to meet its payment obligations under the contracts is largely dependent upon funding from the FEMA or other sources. In the event that PREPA does not pay the remaining amount owed to us under the Settlement Agreement, our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows may be materially and adversely affected.

paragraphs: 本公司為一體化、重視成長的服務公司，主要為客戶提供產品與服務，客戶主要來自石油與天然氣、航空及基礎建設產業。本公司主要業務目標為透過提升執行效率，優先考量資產使用率、邊際利益擴張及資本效率，以提高回報。本公司服務組合包括租賃服務、基礎建設服務、天然石英砂支撐劑服務、住宿服務及鑽井服務。本公司租賃服務分部提供用於油田、建設及航空活動的廣泛設備。本公司基礎建設服務部門為光纖產業提供工程、設計、建設、升級、維護及修繕服務。本公司天然石英砂支撐劑服務部門開採、加工及銷售用於水力壓裂的天然石英砂支撐劑。本公司鑽井服務分部為油田運營商提供導向鑽井服務。本公司相信，我們所提供的服務在提高非常規資源生產流的最終回收量與現值，以及建設與改善光纖網路方面扮演關鍵角色。我們的服務組合提供我們跨銷售服務與擴大客戶羣與地理佈局的機會。
本公司持續著重於成長租賃業務。我們相信，我們的航空資產組合為運營商提供一種有吸引力的航空資產融資形式，使資本部署與機隊靈活性得以實現，同時消除運營商的殘值風險。
本公司設施與服務中心 strategically 位於俄亥俄州、德克薩斯州、奧克拉荷馬州、威斯康辛州及加拿大亞伯塔省，主要用以服務以下地區：
•東俄亥俄州；•南俄亥俄州；•西德克薩斯州；•美國東北部的阿巴拉契亞盆地；•奧克拉荷馬州的SCOOP與STACK地區；
•阿肯色州與奧克拉荷馬州的阿克莫拉盆地；•奧克拉荷馬州的安德爾科盆地；•西弗吉尼亞州與賓夕法尼亞州的馬爾辛頁巖；
•新墨西哥州東南部；•德克薩斯州的巴內特頁巖；•奧克拉荷馬州與德克薩斯州的格蘭特瓦什與密西西比頁巖；
•奧克拉荷馬州的卡納伍德福德與伍德福德頁巖以及克萊弗蘭德砂岩；
本公司營運部門主管擁有廣泛的經驗，平均服務經驗超過29年。他們為本公司帶來寶貴的專業知識與長期客戶關係。本公司為一組多樣化的公眾與私人獨立石油與天然氣生產者、石英砂供應商、光纖網路所有者及以飛機為基礎的乘客與貨運服務提供者提供租賃服務、基礎建設服務、天然石英砂支撐劑、住宿服務及鑽井服務。
本公司之營業收入、營運收入（損失）及可辨認資產主要來自五個應報告分部：租賃服務、基礎建設服務、天然石英砂壓裂服務、住宿服務及鑽井服務。
本公司之設備租賃服務提供用於鑽井、流回與水力壓裂服務以及建設活動之廣泛設備。本公司之設備租賃包括起重機、輕型機械、發電機及其他油田相關設備。本公司於西德州、東俄亥俄州、賓州及西維吉尼亞州提供設備租賃服務。
本公司之航空服務包括向客戶出租飛機及飛機設備。飛機設備包括輔助動力單元（"APUs"）及發動機。截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有九架區域飛機、兩架直升機、五具噴氣發動機及十具APUs。
本公司之基礎建設服務業務提供光纖網路之工程、設計、建設、升級、維護及修理服務。本公司之基礎建設服務主要於美國西南部及中西部地區提供。

自我們從事此業務領域營運以來，我們基礎建設收入的相當大一部分來自風暴復原工程，主要來自波多黎各電力管理局（Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority，或稱 PREPA），由於颶風瑪麗亞（Hurricane Maria）造成的損壞。2017年10月19日，cobra acquisitions llc（或稱 Cobra）與 PREPA 籤訂了一項緊急主服務協議，用以修復 PREPA 的電力網。該一年期的合約（經修正後）允許支付最高達 945 百萬美元。2018年5月26日，Cobra 與 PREPA 籤訂了第二項一年期、900 百萬美元的主服務協議，用以提供額外的修復服務並開始波多黎各電力系統重建的初步階段。我們在與 PREPA 的每項合約下的工作於 2019 年 3 月 31 日結束。PREPA 目前正面臨破產程序，該程序於 2017 年 7 月提出，目前仍在美國波多黎各地區地方法院（"Title III Court"）進行中。因此，PREPA 依上述協議履行付款義務的能力 largely 取決於來自美國國土安全部災難管理署（"FEMA"）或其他來源的資金。自 2019 年 9 月 30 日起，Cobra 已在 Title III Court 及其他爭議解決程序中進行訴訟，以追討 PREPA 應付 Cobra 的波多黎各復原服務費用，有關程序在本公司先前提交給 SEC 的報告中更詳細說明。PREPA 約持有 18.4 百萬美元的資金（"Withheld FEMA Funds"）來自 FEMA，並被認為應支付給 Cobra，但因三個波多黎各市鎮（"Specified Municipalities"）聲請扣押（"Specified Municipal Tax Claims"）某些市鎮稅款而被扣留，而 Cobra 對任何有效的扣押聲請表示異議。

2024年7月22日，Cobra與PREPA及波多黎各財務監督與管理委員會（"FOMB"）簽訂釋放與和解協議，以解決Cobra與PREPA之間所有未結事宜（"和解協議"）。根據和解協議之條款，Cobra被允許對PREPA提出行政費用聲請，總計170.0 百萬美元，加上18.4 百萬美元之被扣留FEMA資金。Cobra之允許聲請將分三期支付：(i) 150.0 百萬美元於Title III法院批准和解協議之較晚日期（A）或2024年8月31日；(ii) 20.0 百萬美元於PREPA調整計畫生效後七日內；(iii) 18.4 百萬美元（需提供一或多份擔保信用狀）之被扣留FEMA資金，於（A）Title III法院對和解命令提出上訴之期限屆滿後十個營業日，或（B）若指定市鎮對和解命令允許PREPA將被扣留FEMA資金釋放給Cobra而不保留對指定市鎮之責任提出上訴，則於上訴通知提出後十個營業日內。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與本年度10-K表報中包含的合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。本討論包含前瞻性陳述，反映本公司目前對可能影響未來營運結果或財務狀況的事件與財務趨勢的預期、估計與假設。實際結果與事件的時程可能因多種因素而與這些前瞻性陳述有重大差異，包括在第1A項「風險因素」及本年度報告中其他部分標題為「前瞻性陳述」的段落中所討論的那些因素。

本公司為一整合性、成長導向的服務公司，主要為客戶提供產品與服務，客戶主要來自石油與天然氣、航空與基礎建設產業。本公司主要業務目標為透過提高執行效率，優先考量資產使用率、邊際擴張與資本效率，以提升回報。本公司服務組合包括租賃服務、基礎建設服務、天然石英砂支撐劑服務、住宿服務與鑽井服務。本公司租賃服務部門提供用於油田、建設與航空活動的廣泛設備。本公司基礎建設服務部門為光纖產業提供工程、設計、建設、升級、維護與修理服務。本公司天然石英砂支撐劑服務部門從事天然石英砂支撐劑的採礦、加工與銷售，此產品用於水力壓裂。本公司鑽井服務部門為油田經營者提供導向鑽井服務。本公司認為，我們所提供的服務在提高非常規資源生產流的最終回收量與現值，以及在建設與改善光纖網路方面扮演關鍵角色。我們的服務組合提供我們跨銷售服務與擴大客戶羣與地理佈局的機會。
本公司持續著力於成長租賃業務。我們認為，我們的航空資產組合為經營者提供一種有吸引力的航空資產融資形式，允許資金部署與機隊靈活性，同時消除經營者殘值風險。
我們的營業收入、營運（虧損）收入與可辨認資產歸屬於五個應報告分部：租賃服務；基礎建設服務；天然石英砂支撐劑服務；住宿服務；以及鑽井服務。因應2025年完成的資產處分，我們的應報告分部已進行調整，因此2024年12月31日財年結的前一年分部資訊已重新整理，以符合目前的分部呈現方式。自以下日期以來，我們透過以下實體進行營運：

headings: 與我們業務及所服務產業相關之風險
我們的客戶集中度高，若失去一個或數個重要客戶，或其未能支付所欠我們的金額，可能會導致我們的營業收入大幅下降。
我們可能因應收帳款備抵減損而產生超過所記錄之損失。
我們的循環信貸協議對我們設有限制，可能影響我們成功運作業務的能力。
油氣產業的週期性可能導致我們的營運成果波動。
若原油價格或天然氣價格下跌，可能會對我們的油氣服務需求產生負面影響。
未能有效且及時應對能源轉型至低碳足跡，可能會對我們的油氣業務產生負面影響。
主要零組件、更換零件或其他設備、物料或材料的短缺、交貨延誤或供應中斷，可能會對我們的租賃業務產生負面影響。
油氣田服務技術的進步可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營業成果及現金流產生重大不利影響。
本公司業務依賴取得第三方供應商提供的專業設備與零件，我們可能面臨交貨延遲及未來價格上漲的風險。
我們可能無法準確估算固定價格合約下基礎設施服務的相關成本，這可能對本公司財務狀況、營業成果及現金流產生不利影響。
我們可能無法取得足夠的擔保能力以支持某些服務方案，且對績效與擔保債券的需求可能降低本公司週轉信用貸款的可用性。
本公司基礎設施服務業務的性質使我們面臨擔保主張及工程瑕疵的潛在責任，這可能降低本公司利潤。
新合約的簽訂時點與現有合約的終止可能導致本公司現金流與財務結果出現不可預測的波動。
對我們砂礦儲量數量與品質的估算不準確，可能導致銷售額低於預期，且生產成本高於預期。
對我們壓裂砂產品的需求可能因井刺激程序與技術的變更，以及政府規範與其他適用法律的變更而減少。
我們在業務中面臨分銷與物流的挑戰。
運輸及相關成本的增加可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
對水資源的取得減少及無法取得或維持必要許可證可能不利於我們的壓裂砂加工廠運作。
我們所提供的與服務的模組化營地因具備客製化特性及遠離主要地區的地理位置，可能帶來獨特的挑戰，這些挑戰可能對我們遠端住宿業務的成功運作產生不利影響。
健康與食品安全問題及食物傳染病的擔憂可能對我們的遠端住宿業務產生不利影響。
加拿大油砂地區或其他我們設立遠端住宿設施的地區若發展出永久基礎設施，可能對我們的遠端住宿業務產生負面影響。
我們遠端住宿業務所產生的收入及產生的費用以加拿大幣計價，可能因貨幣波動而受到負面影響。
在業務運作過程中，我們可能面臨訴訟、賠償或其他聲請，這些可能對我們的業務、營運成果及現金流產生重大且不利的影響。
本公司依賴少數關鍵員工，若這些員工無法繼續服務或離職，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
若本公司無法僱用足夠數量具備技能與資格之工作人員，將可能導致本公司之生產能力與獲利減少，且成長潛力亦可能受損。
工會化努力可能增加本公司之成本或限制本公司之靈活性。
對總體經濟、商業或產業條件之憂慮，可能對本公司之營運成果、流動性及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 下列為我們認為適用於我們業務及我們所從事產業之某些風險。請您仔細考量下列所描述之風險，並配合本年度報告中所提供的財務資料及相關附註，以及我們其他公開揭露資訊。下列所描述之風險突顯了可能對我們業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、流動性及因此而影響我們普通股市場價值之潛在事件、趨勢或其他情況。這些風險可能導致我們未來之結果與歷史結果及我們對未來財務表現之預期有重大差異。下列所描述之風險為我們所識別出之重大風險，並非我們所面臨所有風險之完整清單。未來可能尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為其為不重要，但這些風險也可能對我們未來之業務營運產生重大且不利之影響。請參閱本文件第 iv 頁所載有關前瞻性陳述之說明與限制事項。

當主要客戶停止使用我們之服務時，我們之營收將下降，且營運結果與財務狀況將受損害，除非此損失能被新業務所抵銷。我們前五大客戶於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度分別佔我們營收約 55% 及 58%。我們很可能會在未來繼續從相對少量之客戶取得重大部分之營收。此外，我們因客戶羣集中而面臨信用風險。若我們之交易對手未能履行其義務，包括未能按時或完全支付應付款項，無論是因財務與經濟條件之變動或其他原因，均可能對我們之營運結果產生重大不利影響，並可能影響我們之流動性。
我們根據客戶之付款能力、付款紀錄、經濟事件及其他因素評估應收帳款之可收回性。已記錄之備抵帳準備金為我們對現有應收帳款之當前信用損失之預估，並根據歷史客戶評估、現行財務狀況及合理且可支持之預測所決定。客戶財務狀況之意外變動或未來經濟不確定性，可能導致對特定備抵帳準備金之額外需求，這可能會對我們之業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生重大影響。
我們無法預測烏克蘭戰爭持續進行、中東地區不穩定及美國在委內瑞拉之行動對全球經濟、能源市場、地緣政治穩定、我們所從事產業及我們業務之影響。
俄羅斯與烏克蘭衝突、中東地區不穩定及美國在委內瑞拉之行動之更廣泛後果，可能增加石油與天然氣價格與需求之波動性，這將對油井服務產業產生不利影響，增加遭受網路攻擊之風險，造成全球供應鏈之中斷，增加外幣匯率波動，造成資本市場之限制或中斷，並限制流動性之來源。我們無法預測這些戰爭對我們業務與營運結果之影響程度，以及對全球經濟、能源市場及我們所從事產業之影響。
Cobra 為與 PREPA 簽訂服務合約之一方。由於 PREPA 進行破產程序，PREPA 依合約履行付款義務之能力 largely 依賴於 FEMA 或其他來源之資金。若 PREPA 未支付 Settlement Agreement 下所欠我們之剩餘金額，則我們之財務狀況、營運結果及現金流可能受到重大且不利之影響。
